cells.tense: The understanding is here now, and what you have worked out is doing real work.
cells.ask: Take one pattern you have worked out and write it in five plain sentences with no jargon. Show it to one person. Watch which sentence they ask about.
cells.core:
You have been at the same small work long enough that the shape underneath it is coming clear. That came from repetition, not from a mood — the task kept at until it stopped costing effort and started being sight. It is why what you say lands: the pattern is not borrowed, and people can feel the difference between a phrase and something held.

A clear line of structure can come out of that sight, and someone else can stand on it. The sight is running ahead of the saying now. Keep the practice where it is; let one worked-out pattern leave the bench in words somebody can use.

cells.tense: You are bracing against a version of this that has not happened yet, reading the pattern ahead of the fact.
cells.ask: Pick one pattern you are watching for and write down what evidence would prove it wrong. Then leave it alone for a day and do the next small piece of the work.
cells.core:
The reading has gotten ahead of the thing read. A shape starts forming and it is already a prediction — what that person is doing, what this is really about, what is coming — and the shapes arrive faster than anything can confirm them.

Direction does not survive that much looking ahead. Give the pattern one container, write it in a form that can be checked later, and let the check wait. The practice still knows the way back, and what is short here is not certainty. It is a next piece small enough to finish today, and one container the pattern stays inside.

cells.tense: You stopped at the surface a while back, and you are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.ask: Ask one person who has done the work longer than you to walk you through something they know. Do it as a learner, ask questions, and keep what they say about their own practice.
cells.core:
You are taking the world literally and on purpose. A story is a story, a symbol is decoration, a rule is a rule — nothing underneath is being looked for, and the bench has gone quiet. What stopped is not the work. It is the reaching under it.

A person in good shape here sees one thing clearly and can tell you what it does — the shape of a problem, the way a routine actually moves — and then puts that shape to work in the next small task. What is missing now is company: someone who has walked the thing and can say out loud how it is done. The way back runs through them, not through you pushing alone, and one question asked to the right person asks a different question in you.

cells.tense: You are already running the pattern in how you spend your days, and you would not say you are.
cells.ask: Say out loud what your practice has actually taught you. One sentence. Say it as yours, not as just the way things are.
cells.core:
Day after day at the same work taught you a shape — how things move, what makes one of them come out right, what matters underneath. Your choices run on it. But you describe it as just how things are, what anyone would do in your place. That is the pattern steering you while you call it the ground you stand on.

The understanding is real and the practice that built it is real. Only the ownership is missing. Say the thing once as yours — no hedge on it, no 'well, anyone would' attached — and the ground under the practice starts being ground you stand on deliberately, one sentence at a time.

attempts.check: The record does not say the person's solitude has served them or that their practice habitually works; it only says focused cultivation is the seat, so 'it's working' must be described as something visible now, not asserted as history. A reader could fairly say the pattern-seeing is just careful thinking or that the solitude is simply how the work gets done, not a hiding place. The ask survives that objection because it produces a small visible trace of the pattern either way, and the sentence that serves me — 'you already see it' — is cut before the cells are written.
